name: Slide 16A: Synthetic Events & Event Handling in React
shortTitle: Event Handling & Synthetic Events in React
qText: What are Synthetic Events and Event Delegation in React?
bullets: Cross-Browser Wrapper: SyntheticEvent wraps native browser events so they work identically across Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge.
Event Delegation: React doesn't attach handlers to individual DOM nodes. It attaches a single listener to the root container (#root in React 17+).
Performance Gain: Attaching 1,000 click listeners to 1,000 table rows uses negligible memory because of root delegation.
Return False Doesn't Work: You must call e.preventDefault() explicitly; return false does not prevent default in React.

name: Slide 27B: Component Composition & State Lifting
shortTitle: Component Composition & State Lifting
qText: How does State Lifting & Component Composition work?
bullets: Single Source of Truth: When two sibling components need to share the same data, lift state up to their closest common parent.
Unidirectional Flow: Parent holds the state, passes data down via props, and passes callback functions down for children to trigger updates.
Component Composition: Use children prop to compose components instead of hardcoded prop drilling.
Avoid Direct Mutation: Always update state with immutable copies (spread operator [...arr], {...obj}).

name: Slide 27C: Immutable State Updates & Why Mutation is Evil
shortTitle: Immutable State Updates & Why Mutation Fails
qText: Why is Direct State Mutation Wrong in React?
bullets: Referential Comparison: React checks Object.is(oldState, newState). Direct mutation keeps the exact same memory pointer, so React assumes nothing changed and skips re-rendering!
Time-Travel & DevTools Broken: Direct mutation overwrites the past state history in memory, breaking undo/redo and debugging.
Async Race Conditions: React batches updates. Mutating state causes concurrent readers to see half-mutated data.
Golden Rule: Always return a newly created object or array using spread {...old}, [...old], or Immer.

name: Slide 8A: React Rendering Lifecycle: Trigger ➔ Render ➔ Commit
shortTitle: Trigger ➔ Render ➔ Commit Lifecycle
qText: What are the 3 Phases: Trigger ➔ Render ➔ Commit?
bullets: Step 1: Trigger: Initial mount or state update (setState) schedules a render task with the scheduler.
Step 2: Render (Reconciliation): React invokes component functions, constructs the new Virtual DOM, and diffs with previous tree. Pure calculation with zero DOM mutations.
Step 3: Commit Phase: React touches the browser DOM. Applies calculated mutations (insert, update, delete). Synchronous and atomic.
Browser Paint: After commit, browser recalculates layout (Reflow) and paints pixels onto the screen.

name: Slide 8B: React Fiber Architecture & Fiber Nodes
shortTitle: React Fiber Architecture & Linked List Tree
qText: What is React Fiber and Fiber Node structure?
bullets: Why Fiber? Old React (Stack reconciler) was recursive and synchronous; large trees blocked the browser main thread and dropped frames.
Fiber Node: Fiber turns the call stack into a linked-list data structure that can be paused, prioritized, and resumed.
Pointers: Every Fiber node holds 3 pointers: child (first child), sibling (next sibling), and return (parent).
Time-Slicing: Fiber breaks heavy rendering into 5ms chunks. High priority tasks (keystrokes) jump ahead of low priority tasks (lists).

name: Slide 8C: Fiber Double Buffering & Tree Swapping
shortTitle: Current Tree vs Work-in-Progress Tree
qText: How does Double Buffering prevent UI flickering?
bullets: Current Tree: The Fiber tree currently visible and mounted on the browser screen.
Work-in-Progress (WIP) Tree: Built asynchronously in background RAM during the Render Phase.
Instant Pointer Swap: On Commit, React swaps root.current = workInProgress in a single pointer operation (0ms latency).
No Half-Baked UI: If a render is aborted due to an error, the WIP tree is discarded and the user sees no broken screen!

name: Slide 8D: Keys & Component Identity during Reconciliation
shortTitle: Keys & Component Identity during Reconciliation
qText: How do Keys determine Component Identity & Re-renders?
bullets: Component Identity: React uses element.type and key to decide whether to reuse an existing DOM node or destroy and recreate it.
Same Key, Same Position: React updates props and preserves existing local state and focus.
Different Key: React unmounts old component (runs cleanup), destroys state, and mounts fresh instance.
Resetting State Trick: Passing key={userId} to a form component automatically resets all its local state when the user changes without any useEffect!

name: Slide 8E: React Strict Mode & Double Rendering Behavior
shortTitle: Strict Mode & Intentional Double Invocation
qText: Why does Strict Mode render twice in development?
bullets: Development Only: Double rendering only happens in development (npm run dev). Never occurs in production builds!
Why? Catching Impure Code: React intentionally mounts ➔ unmounts ➔ mounts components to verify that cleanup functions work.
Side-Effect Detection: If your component or reducer mutates global variables, running twice immediately exposes the bug.
Production Zero Overhead: StrictMode does not produce any visible UI elements or runtime overhead in production.

qText: When should you use useReducer instead of useState?
bullets: Complex State Logic: When state involves multiple sub-values, nested objects, or when the next state depends on the previous state.
Decoupled Actions: Separates 'what happened' (dispatch action) from 'how state updates' (reducer function).
Passing Dispatch Down: Dispatch function has a stable identity and never changes across re-renders, optimizing child component performance.
Mini-Redux locally: Provides Redux-like predictable state management within a single component tree without adding external packages.

name: Slide 76C: useTransition vs useDeferredValue in React 18
shortTitle: useTransition vs useDeferredValue (Concurrent)
qText: How do useTransition & useDeferredValue optimize UI responsiveness?
bullets: Urgent vs Transition: Urgent updates (typing input, clicking tabs) need instant response. Transition updates (filtering 5,000 items) can lag without blocking the UI.
useTransition: Wraps a state setter: startTransition(() => setQuery(text)). Gives isPending spinner indicator.
useDeferredValue: Wraps a value directly: const deferredQuery = useDeferredValue(query). Defers re-rendering dependent components.
Result: Search typing never stutters, even while filtering massive datasets!

name: Slide 76D: useId Hook: Accessible Unique IDs in SSR & CSR
shortTitle: useId Hook for Accessible Forms
qText: What is the role of useId hook in React 18?
bullets: The Problem: Hardcoding id='email' breaks when a component renders multiple times on the same page. Math.random() causes SSR hydration mismatch errors!
The Solution: useId() generates a unique, stable string ID that matches 100% identically on both Server and Client.
Accessibility (a11y): Perfect for linking <label htmlFor={id}> to <input id={id}> and aria-describedby.

name: Slide 81A: Derived State: Don't Store What You Can Compute
shortTitle: Derived State Pattern vs Redundant State
qText: Why is Derived State better than synchronizing state?
bullets: The Anti-Pattern: Creating state for items list AND separate state for filteredItems or totalPrice, then syncing them with useEffect.
Why it Fails: Causes out-of-sync bugs, requires multiple re-renders, and bloats component code.
The Rule: If a value can be computed from existing props or state, compute it on-the-fly during render (wrap in useMemo if expensive)!

name: Slide 81B: Debouncing vs Throttling in API Integration
shortTitle: Debouncing vs Throttling Comparison
qText: What is the difference between Debouncing and Throttling?
tableRows: Delays execution until user **stops typing** for N ms
Executes function at most once every N ms interval
Fires at fixed periodic rate during continuous activity
Window scrolling, game loop, mouse move
Saves 95% of unnecessary network API calls
Ensures smooth UI updates without freezing thread

name: Slide 81C: Authentication Flow & Axios Interceptor Handling
shortTitle: Auth Flow & Axios Interceptors
qText: How do Axios Interceptors handle JWT Expiry & Refresh Tokens?
bullets: Request Interceptor: Automatically injects Authorization: Bearer token header into every outgoing HTTP request.
Response Interceptor: Listens for HTTP 401 Unauthorized response.
Silent Refresh: Catches 401, calls /auth/refresh endpoint to get fresh access token, updates headers, and replays the original failed request seamlessly!
Logout Fallback: If refresh token is also expired, clears session storage and redirects to /login.

name: Slide 124A: Referential Equality & Stable References
shortTitle: Referential Equality & Stable Object References
qText: Why does Referential Equality break React.memo?
bullets: Memory Reference Check: JavaScript compares objects and functions by memory address, not value ({} !== {}).
Re-creation on Render: Every time a parent renders, inline objects style={{color:'red'}} and inline functions () => doWork() are given new memory addresses.
React.memo Breakdown: React.memo does shallow equality (oldProp === newProp). Since pointers differ, it re-renders the child anyway!
The Fix: Use useCallback for callbacks and useMemo for objects passed to memoized children.

name: Slide 124B: Context API Re-render Trap & Split Context Solution
shortTitle: Split Context Pattern for Performance
qText: How to fix the Context API Re-render Trap?
bullets: The Flaw: In Context API, all components calling useContext(MyContext) re-render whenever ANY value in the context object changes.
The Scenario: A component that only dispatches an action still re-renders whenever state changes if both are in the same context!
The Architecture Fix: Split into two contexts: StateContext (for data consumers) and DispatchContext (for action triggers).

name: Slide 116A: Error Boundaries in React
shortTitle: Error Boundaries Architecture & Fallback UI
qText: What are Error Boundaries & How do they prevent White Screen of Death?
bullets: The Problem: In React 16+, an uncaught JavaScript error in any component unmounts the entire component tree, causing a completely blank white screen.
Error Boundary: A class component that catches JavaScript errors anywhere in its child component tree and displays a fallback UI.
Lifecycle Methods: Uses static getDerivedStateFromError() to render fallback UI and componentDidCatch() to log error telemetry (Sentry).

name: Slide 116B: React Portals for Modals, Tooltips & Dialogs
shortTitle: React Portals (`createPortal`) Pattern
qText: Why and when should you use ReactDOM.createPortal?
bullets: CSS Overflow / z-index Trap: When a modal is rendered inside a parent with overflow: hidden or complex z-index stacking, the modal gets clipped.
Portal Solution: ReactDOM.createPortal(children, domNode) inserts the modal directly into document.body outside the parent DOM hierarchy.
React Event Bubbling Preserved: Even though the DOM node lives in document.body, React events bubble up the React component tree naturally!

name: Slide 116C: forwardRef & useImperativeHandle
shortTitle: forwardRef & useImperativeHandle Pattern
qText: How does forwardRef pass refs to child components?
bullets: By Default: Functional components cannot receive a ref prop from their parent.
forwardRef: Wraps a functional component to expose its underlying DOM element (e.g. <input>) to a parent ref.
useImperativeHandle: Customizes the instance value that is exposed to parent components, restricting access to safe public methods only (e.g. focus(), reset()).

shortTitle: Nested Routes & Outlet in React Router v6
qText: How do Nested Routes and <Outlet /> work in React Router v6?
bullets: Layout Persistence: Allows shared UI (like Sidebar, Navigation Header) to stay mounted without re-rendering while sub-pages switch inside.
The <Outlet /> Component: Placed inside the parent layout component as a placeholder where child route components are dynamically injected.
Clean URL Mapping: /dashboard loads layout; /dashboard/patients loads child view inside the Outlet.

name: Slide 64B: Protected Routes & Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
shortTitle: Protected Routes & Role-Based Access Control
qText: How to implement Protected Routes and RBAC in React?
bullets: Authentication Check: If token is missing, redirect unauthenticated user to /login using <Navigate to='/login' replace />.
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Check user's assigned role (e.g. 'Admin' | 'Doctor' | 'Nurse') against allowed roles array.
Unauthorized Redirect: If authenticated but wrong permissions, redirect to /unauthorized page.

name: Slide 64C: Feature-Based Enterprise Folder Architecture
shortTitle: Feature-Based Enterprise Folder Structure
qText: What is the industry standard Folder Structure for React?
bullets: Feature-Based Organization: Group files by business feature rather than technical type (e.g. all patient files live under features/patients/).
Colocation Principle: Keep components, tests, hooks, and API queries together in the same feature folder.
Shared Layer: Generic UI buttons, headers, and utility helpers live in src/components/ and src/utils/.
code:
src/
├── api/             # Global Axios client & base endpoints
├── assets/          # Static images, svg icons
├── components/      # Generic shared UI (Button, Modal, Table)
├── features/        # Business Domains:
│   ├── auth/        # Auth slices, login components, auth hooks
│   └── patients/    # PatientList, PatientCard, usePatientQuery
├── hooks/           # App-wide custom hooks (useDebounce, useWindowSize)
├── routes/          # App router configuration & ProtectedRoutes
└── store/           # Redux configureStore & rootReducer

name: Slide 120A: XSS Attacks, dangerouslySetInnerHTML & DOMPurify
shortTitle: XSS Attacks & dangerouslySetInnerHTML Security
qText: How does React prevent XSS & how to safely render HTML?
bullets: Automatic String Escaping: React automatically escapes all strings rendered inside JSX expressions ({userInput}) into safe strings, neutralizing injection attacks.
The Danger Zone: dangerouslySetInnerHTML bypasses React escaping. If an attacker injects <script> or <img onerror='evil()'>, it executes!
Production Sanitization: Always sanitize raw HTML using DOMPurify before feeding it to dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

name: Slide 122A: React Testing Library (RTL) vs Jest Testing Philosophy
shortTitle: React Testing Library vs Jest Testing Philosophy
qText: What is the testing philosophy of React Testing Library?
bullets: Guiding Principle: 'The more your tests resemble the way your software is used, the more confidence they can give you.'
No Implementation Details: Never test internal state variables or private methods. Test what the user sees and clicks!
User-Centric Queries: Prefer getByRole('button', { name: /save/i }) and getByLabelText() over brittle CSS class selectors or test IDs.

name: Slide 10.1: Redux Fundamentals & Architecture Flow
shortTitle: Redux Architecture & Complete Unidirectional Data Flow
qText: What is Redux and the Complete Data Flow?
bullets: Single Source of Truth: Entire global state of the app is stored in an object tree inside a single Store.
State is Read-Only: The only way to change state is to emit an Action (an object describing what happened).
Pure Reducer Functions: Reducers take (previousState, action) => newState and must be 100% pure with 0 side-effects.
Unidirectional Flow: UI Event ➔ dispatch(action) ➔ Reducer calculates new state ➔ Store updates ➔ Subscribed UI re-renders!

name: Slide 10.2: Redux vs Context API Decision Matrix
shortTitle: Redux vs Context API Decision Matrix
qText: When to use Redux vs Context API?
tableRows: All consumers re-render when context changes
Only components selecting changed state re-render
Redux is much faster for large apps
Time-travel debugging, action logs, state diff

name: Slide 10.3: When to Use Redux vs When NOT to Use Redux
shortTitle: When to Use Redux vs When NOT to Use Redux
qText: When should you use Redux and when is it Overkill?
bullets: DO Use Redux When: Large app with complex state shared across multiple unrelated components; frequent state updates; team needs predictable architecture and time-travel DevTools.
DON'T Use Redux When: Simple CRUD apps; simple forms (use local state / React Hook Form); purely server cache (use React Query or RTK Query directly); theme/auth only (use Context API).

name: Slide 11.1: Redux Toolkit (RTK) configureStore & createSlice
shortTitle: configureStore & createSlice Architecture
qText: How does createSlice eliminate boilerplate?
bullets: No Action Creators Needed: createSlice automatically generates action creators and action type strings from reducer names.
Immer Built-in: You write code that looks like direct mutation (state.count += 1), but Immer safely produces a new immutable copy!
configureStore: Automatically sets up Redux DevTools, Redux Thunk, and combines reducers with zero manual config.

name: Slide 11.2: Typed Hooks: useAppDispatch & useAppSelector
shortTitle: Typed Hooks with TypeScript in RTK
qText: Why create custom useAppDispatch and useAppSelector?
bullets: The Problem: Standard useSelector requires importing (state: RootState) on every single component call.
Typed Hooks Solution: Export pre-typed hooks once in app/hooks.ts.
Safety & Autocomplete: Provides 100% autocompletion for state keys and guarantees thunk action types for dispatch.

name: Slide 12.1: createAsyncThunk & extraReducers Lifecycle
shortTitle: createAsyncThunk & extraReducers Lifecycle
qText: How does createAsyncThunk handle API lifecycles?
bullets: Why Not in Reducers? Reducers must remain 100% synchronous and pure. Async operations belong in Thunk middleware.
Automatic 3 States: Generates pending, fulfilled, and rejected action types automatically.
extraReducers: Slice listens to thunk actions using the builder callback syntax.

name: Slide 12.2: dispatch().unwrap() & Error Handling in UI
shortTitle: dispatch().unwrap() Pattern in Components
qText: Why is .unwrap() needed when dispatching thunks?
bullets: Thunk Always Resolves: Redux Thunk always returns a resolved promise by default (even when rejected) so that middleware doesn't crash.
The Component Problem: A standard try / catch block in your component will NOT catch a rejected thunk!
The Solution (.unwrap()): Calling dispatch(thunk()).unwrap() extracts the raw payload or throws a real JavaScript error for the component's catch block.

name: Slide 13.1: RTK Query: Automated Caching & Tags Invalidation
shortTitle: RTK Query: Auto Caching & Tags Invalidation
qText: How does RTK Query manage server cache & invalidation?
bullets: Server State vs Client State: APIs are server cache, not client UI state. RTK Query manages data fetching, caching, and deduplication automatically.
Auto-generated Hooks: useGetPatientsQuery() gives data, isLoading, isError, refetch instantly.
Tags Cache Invalidation: Query provides tags (providesTags: ['Patients']). Mutation invalidates tags (invalidatesTags: ['Patients']), which automatically refetches data!

name: Slide 13.2: Optimistic Updates & Instant UI Feedback in RTK Query
shortTitle: Optimistic Updates with Rollback
qText: How to implement Optimistic Updates with rollback in RTK Query?
bullets: Immediate UI Update: Update the client cache immediately before the backend server responds to make the app feel instant.
Lifecycle Hook: Use onQueryStarted in the mutation endpoint.
Automatic Rollback: If the backend request fails, the catch block calls patchResult.undo(), restoring the original state instantly.
